payload.objective: Assess whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can support human voriconazole exposure prediction and efficacious-dose estimation (SC001).

context_sources.main:/objective: Assess whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can support human voriconazole exposure prediction and efficacious-dose estimation (SC001).
context_sources.main:/study/regimen: Multiple source-specific animal regimens and planned human IV and oral regimens, including loading doses; details remain study-specific (SC005, SC007, SC009, SC010, SC011, SC014, SC023).
context_sources.main:/study/population: Primary mouse and rat studies; secondary multi-species evidence; in-vitro fungal susceptibility data; independent human validation (SC003–SC018).
context_sources.main:/study/system: Animal systemic PK and organism- and endpoint-specific antifungal PK/PD, translated to human plasma exposure (SC005–SC018, SC023–SC026).
context_sources.main:/study/measurements: Concentrations, PK parameters and exposures, isolate efficacy, survival ED50s, protein binding and MICs (SC005–SC018, SC030).
context_sources.main:/study/methods: Planned preparation, animal PK modeling, human translation, PK/PD index comparison, independent validation and PTA analysis (SC021–SC026).
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/0/stateme: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human voriconazole exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation. The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/1/stateme: Voriconazole is the sole test drug. Fluconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, amphotericin B, caspofungin and tofacitinib appear as comparators or co-administered drugs and must not substitute for it.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/2/stateme: The proposal is Animal to Human Translation of Voriconazole, feasibility study Version 1.0 (draft), dated 9 October 2026. Voriconazole is a known-drug test case with existing human PK intended for independent validation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/3/stateme: Voriconazole_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes rather than a ready-made modeling dataset; these are proposal-described resource roles, not inspected attachment contents.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/4/stateme: The Mouse sheet is described as containing digitized mean plasma curves and exposure parameters after oral doses in non-neutropenic aspergillosis mice.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/5/stateme: The Mouse sheet is described as containing serum PK parameters and per-isolate efficacy in neutropenic candidiasis mice.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/6/stateme: The Mouse sheet is described as containing intraperitoneal PK and survival ED50s against A. flavus.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/7/stateme: The Mouse sheet is described as containing serum levels in mice given grapefruit juice.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/8/stateme: Two mouse studies sampled PK on treatment day 2; the proposal does not identify those studies individually.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/9/stateme: The Rat sheet is described as containing single IV and oral PK with and without a co-administered drug.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/10/statem: A rat population model describes saturable elimination and autoinduction from 10-day intraperitoneal dosing.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/11/statem: The rat AUCs associated with SC011 are model-predicted.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/12/statem: The Rat sheet also describes a population model with plasma binding in healthy and meningitis rats.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/13/statem: Cross_species_secondary contains one multi-species table for mouse, rat, rabbit, guinea pig and dog, reproduced in a thesis from Roffey et al. (2003). It describes single- and multiple-dose AUC after IV and oral dosing and protein binding; decimals use Portuguese commas. Provenance and mapping issues are MI001 and MI002.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/14/statem: Use SC014 only as low-confidence context or for sensitivity analysis, never as the sole basis for a species model; retain its secondary label throughout.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/15/statem: In_vitro_MIC contains EUCAST MIC distributions for C. albicans and A. fumigatus and isolate MICs for the two mouse aspergillosis studies. Candidiasis isolate MICs are located with their efficacy table on the Mouse sheet.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/16/statem: Use matched isolate MICs for PD and MIC distributions for population-weighted attainment; a distribution cannot replace matched isolate MICs.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/17/statem: The separate human reference file is described as containing label PK parameters and statements, a healthy-volunteer IV-to-oral dose-escalation study, and a human-target column removed from a rat source. Its access restriction is MI003.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/18/statem: Voriconazole_project_proposal.docx defines the task; AGENT_README.md explains package use and known gaps.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/19/statem: The designated uses are mouse PK and eligible PD analysis, and rat systemic PK, nonlinearity and time-dependent clearance.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/20/statem: Planned preparation splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs; checks provenance, units, dose histories, treatment day, analytes, matrices, assays, experimental units and missing fields; and identifies usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/21/statem: Planned animal PK work selects eligible systemic models for mouse and rat, including saturable elimination and time-dependent clearance where supported. It evaluates fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits, and documents whether and how SC014 is used.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/22/statem: Planned human translation uses supported animal models, body size, protein binding, metabolic clearance and justified physiological relationships, accounting for nonlinearity and autoinduction before scaling. It compares approaches with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better; predicts human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses; and freezes those predictions before opening human outcomes.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/23/statem: For eligible data, planned PK/PD analysis compares fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression separately by organism and endpoint. It estimates supported exposure targets or reports that the available data cannot determine a best index or target.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/24/statem: Planned human validation applies the frozen model to doses and regimens in the human reference tables, comparing predicted with observed plasma PK, including the change from single to repeated dosing. It reports bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/25/statem: After PK validation and PD qualification, planned simulation uses a prespecified human population and IV and oral scenarios to estimate PTA at each MIC, reporting distribution-weighted attainment separately. Where supported, it includes an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate with uncertainty. Deliverables are PTA tables/curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/26/statem: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters, model-predicted AUCs and digitized points are not individual animals or observations. Do not invent IDs, exposure-response links or missing measurements; the variability restriction is SC038.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/27/statem: Keep oral gavage, intraperitoneal and IV routes separate; distinguish total from unbound drug, serum from plasma from free brain dialysate, and bioassay from chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Separate neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals. Every conversion requires a recorded justification.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/28/statem: Mouse exposure is reported to rise more than dose-proportionally. Exposure is reported as nonlinear and falling with repeated dosing in mice and rats.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/29/statem: Reported binding descriptions are mouse 78% bound in serum, 29.97% unbound in plasma and 67% in the secondary table, and rat 64-66%. The proposal does not further qualify the percentage basis of the latter two descriptions. The source-declared conflict is MI004.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/30/statem: Never average the conflicting binding sources; carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/31/statem: Give all three indices and both regression families in SC024 equal eligibility. Compare them using the same matched response records, isolate MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/32/statem: Kidney CFU and survival endpoints are not interchangeable. Keep CFU-based and survival-based targets separate; a target from one organism or endpoint cannot set another.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/33/statem: The rat escalating regimen was designed to match a human exposure target; the proposal does not identify it here as a specific regimen in another source block.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/34/statem: Published ED50s, exposure indices and conclusions cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings. Do not use the rat escalating regimen in SC034 to tune scaling, or human outcomes to tune the animal model or scaling. Model/prediction freezing and validation-criterion timing are specified in SC023 and SC025; freeze PD targets and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/35/statem: The EUCAST distributions were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs; the C. albicans data are mostly truncated at 0.016 mg/L.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/36/statem: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators, censored categories and test method (EUCAST, CLSI or NCCLS). Do not interpret SC036 as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize. The distinction between per-MIC PTA and MIC-weighted attainment is retained in SC026.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/37/statem: Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty. Do not invent variability, including interindividual variability from group summaries.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/38/statem: A successful fit is not predictive validation; human PK agreement does not validate antifungal efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/39/statem: Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results, and obtain human review before fitting.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/40/statem: The proposal cites Sou T et al., Model-Informed Drug Development for Antimicrobials: Translational PK and PK/PD Modeling to Predict an Efficacious Human Dose for Apramycin, Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics, 2021;109:1063-1073, https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.2104.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/41/statem: Follow the translational objective of Sou et al. (2021), identified in SC041, without importing the apramycin model or its parameters.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/impact: Primary-source verification of the secondary table cannot be established from the supplied proposal.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/why_it: The proposal explicitly reports that the original Roffey et al. paper was unavailable; attachment registration supplies no additional verification.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/clarif: Provide authorized original-source evidence if available, or retain the provenance limitation under SC015.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/impact: Secondary-table values cannot be assigned confidently to species.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/why_it: The proposal explicitly states that the mapping is unverified.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/clarif: Verify the mapping from authorized evidence before assigning values to species; otherwise preserve the uncertainty and SC015 restrictions.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/impact: Independent human validation must await the authorized release.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/why_it: Human validation data are not in the supplied package. The separate reference file described in SC018 is released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/clarif: Release the separate human reference file only at the specified stage after the required freezes; do not access its outcomes earlier.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/field: Conflicting mouse binding sources and percentage interpretation
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/impact: A single defensible mouse free-exposure conversion cannot be selected from the proposal alone.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/why_it: The source explicitly identifies conflicting binding descriptions in SC030 across serum, plasma and the secondary table; their concentration bases must remain distinct.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/clarif: Resolve source-specific binding definitions and applicability, retaining unresolved alternatives under SC031 rather than averaging them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/impact: A usable modeling dataset and its unresolved record-level limitations have not been established by this transformation.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/why_it: SC021 requires a later preparation assessment. Only the proposal was supplied; attachment bodies were not searched or assessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/clarif: Perform the authorized SC021 assessment and document eligible records and independently identified gaps without assuming completeness.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/field: Animal PK model support and design-permitted evaluation
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/impact: Supported mouse and rat model structures and permitted predictive checks cannot yet be determined.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/why_it: SC022 makes model choices and evaluation conditional on data and design support; the proposal does not supply that assessment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/clarif: Assess the prepared evidence for the conditional choices in SC022 and retain unsupported or unassessable components as limitations.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/impact: Individual variability cannot be used defensibly in animal modeling or carried into human simulations until its evidential basis is established.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/why_it: The proposal distinguishes summaries and predictions from individual observations and prohibits invented variability in SC027 and SC038; attachment-level support remains unassessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/clarif: Determine whether authorized individual-level evidence supports variability estimation; otherwise preserve the limitation without constructing variability from summaries.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/field: Supported human translation inputs and relationships
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/impact: A justified human scaling approach cannot yet be selected.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/why_it: The proposal specifies the translation considerations in SC023 but leaves their supported implementation to later assessment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/clarif: Establish and document the supported inputs and physiological relationships for SC023, including how nonlinearity and autoinduction are addressed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/impact: Prospective human exposure profiles cannot be generated for reproducibly specified dosing histories.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/why_it: The proposal supplies partial regimen components in SC023 but no numerical doses, dosing intervals, loading schedules or treatment durations for those prospective predictions.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/clarif: Specify the complete prospective dosing histories, preserving the distinct routes and loading components already stated in SC023.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/impact: Comparable index regressions and supported targets cannot yet be established.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/why_it: SC024 and SC032 depend on eligibility and matched inputs. The proposal describes relevant resources but does not establish record-level matching or adequacy; attachment bodies were not assessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/clarif: Establish eligible matched records for each organism and endpoint under SC017, SC032 and SC033, or document why an index or target is not determinable.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/impac: Index comparison cannot proceed with a fully registered selection procedure.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/why_i: SC032 requires registration before fitting, but the proposal does not state the selection rule.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/clari: Register the selection rule before index fitting while preserving the comparison requirements and no-forced-winner condition in SC032.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/impac: Human predictive performance cannot receive a prespecified acceptance judgment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/why_i: SC025 names evaluation outputs and requires criteria fixed before validation, but the criteria themselves are not supplied.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/clari: Specify and freeze the validation criteria before evaluating human outcomes; do not derive them from validation results.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/field: MIC distribution preparation and probability support
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/impac: A transparent MIC probability input for later weighted attainment has not been established.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/why_i: The source describes the distribution limitations in SC036 and processing obligations in SC037, but the supplied proposal does not assess the underlying bins, denominators or censored-category handling.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/clari: Assess the authorized MIC tables and document how probabilities preserve the source categories and truncation, without silent renormalization.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/impac: PTA simulation lacks a defined target population.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/why_i: SC026 requires a prespecified human population, but the proposal does not define it.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/clari: Specify the human PTA population before simulation, with variability and uncertainty supported under SC038.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/impac: PTA simulation lacks a reproducible set of dosing scenarios.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/why_i: SC026 specifies route categories but does not supply the numerical PTA scenario choices; these are a separate decision from the prospective prediction regimens in MI009.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/clari: Prespecify the complete PTA dosing scenarios before simulation and document their relationship to the validated PK predictions.

project_rules.text: R004: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. project_rules.text: R005: Keep routes, total and unbound drug, serum, plasma and free brain dialysate, and bioassay and chromatographic results separate. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; do not transfer parameters between doses or days because exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Record a justification for every conversion.

evidence.quote: Separate routes (oral gavage, intraperitoneal, IV), total versus unbound drug, serum versus plasma versus free brain dialysate, and bioassay versus chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats, so parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Every conversion requires a recorded justification.

project_rules.text: R006: Never average the conflicting binding sources: mouse 78% bound in serum, 29.97% unbound in plasma and 67% in the secondary table; rat 64–66%. Carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

evidence.quote: Binding sources conflict (mouse 78% bound in serum versus 29.97% unbound in plasma versus 67% in the secondary table; rat 64-66%); never average them, and carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

library.interpretation: These profiles are project-designed summaries informed by the cited sources, not verbatim guidance or universal regulatory requirements. Use only assigned profiles and assess applicability against the project objective and published rules. Profiles marked DATA_REQUIREMENTS_ONLY report source-backed input coverage and gaps; they do not select analytical methods or qualify results. Prior analytical guidance is retained separately for downstream review and is not loaded into this stage. A profile cannot authorize source access, publish project rules, approve an analysis or impose an unreviewed numeric cutoff. No historical assessment or approval is refreshed automatically. data_roles and condition_triggers let host code map DC labels onto the conditions of profiles already selected from the objective; data never select a profile. A trigger with review OBJECTIVE or DATA, or an undecided label, leaves applicability to the independent coverage review.

sources.supports: Question-specific intended use, criteria, assumptions and fit-for-purpose evaluation; no fixed species-count rule is imported.

sources.title: Phoenix: Lambda Z or Slope Estimation settings
sources.locator: Limitations of Lambda Z and slope estimation
sources.supports: Parameters independent of terminal slope remain reportable when slope estimation fails. Software point-count settings are not universal scientific sufficiency criteria.

sources.title: Phoenix: NCA parameter formulas
sources.locator: Discrete plasma parameters; extrapolation; extravascular clearance/volume footnote
sources.supports: Endpoint-specific input dependencies and distinction between absolute parameters and apparent parameters containing F.

sources.title: Bailer (1988): Testing for the equality of area under the curves when using destructive measurement techniques
sources.supports: Group-level AUC estimation under destructive sampling; not reconstruction of individual trajectories.

sources.title: Tang et al. (2007): Interspecies prediction of human drug clearance based on scaling data from one or two animal species
sources.supports: Calibrated one-/two-species approaches have method-specific evidence. This does not authorize arbitrary fixed exponents or make a species count a validation result.

sources.title: Ring et al. (2011): PhRMA CPCDC initiative, part 3: prediction methods of human clearance
sources.supports: Allometry and IVIVE require different inputs and binding conventions. IV CL comparison involved 19 drugs; applicability to a new drug remains to be assessed.

sources.title: EMA: Use of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in development of antimicrobial medicinal products
sources.locator: Nonclinical PK-PD studies; PK-PD targets and target attainment
sources.supports: Antimicrobial exposure, susceptibility and effect must be linked for the intended use; in vitro and animal infection models can contribute complementary evidence.

sources.title: Bakker-Woudenberg IAJM, ten Kate MT, Goessens WHF, Mouton JW (2006): Effect of treatment duration on pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic indices correlating with therapeutic efficacy of ceftazidime in experimental Klebsiella pneumoniae lung infection
sources.supports: Index conclusions depend on treatment duration and the response endpoint; the rat-model design varied total dose and dosing interval (every 6, 12 or 24 h). Do not transplant the study's winning index or numeric target into another project.

sources.title: Phoenix: PK model options
sources.supports: Compartmental representations require structural and dosing parameters; choosing parameterization is an explicit modeling decision.

sources.title: Heinzl (1996): A note on testing areas under the curve when using destructive measurement techniques
sources.supports: Mean-curve AUC and its variance depend on sampling design and available summaries. The paper corrects an earlier testing approximation; no inferential procedure is automatically adopted by this profile.

sources.title: PKNCA: AUC integration methods
sources.locator: Integration before Tlast; AUClast, AUCall and AUCinf definitions
sources.supports: Integration and extrapolation choices are explicit settings. Package defaults are not project approval or universal requirements.

sources.title: PKNCA: Handle BLQ values in concentration measurements
sources.locator: Details: missing-value handling and first, middle and last BLQ values
sources.supports: Missingness and BLQ handling interact with curve position and require specification. Package input encoding does not authorize overwriting original censoring information.

sources.title: Phoenix: Sparse sampling (pre-clinical) data
sources.locator: Mean Curve Final Parameters and SE_AUClast/SE_AUCall limitations
sources.supports: Mean-curve parameters have a group-level estimand. The documented sparse-AUC standard-error method depends on a linear combination of means and is not automatically applicable to logarithmic trapezoids.

sources.title: Cheng and Jusko (1988): Mean Residence Time Concepts for Pharmacokinetic Systems with Nonlinear Drug Elimination Described by the Michaelis-Menten Equation
sources.supports: For the studied Michaelis-Menten systems, Dose/AUC is a time-average clearance and AUMC/AUC differs from true MRT. This supports an applicability check, not a prohibition on descriptive AUC under all nonlinear conditions.

sources.title: Lee et al. (2021): Pharmacokinetic Characterization of LW6, a Novel Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) Inhibitor in Mice
sources.supports: Metabolite exposure after parent dosing was distinguished from disposition after direct metabolite dosing. Formation calculations used analyte-specific clearance and molecular-weight conversion. No drug-specific parameter is transferred.

sources.title: Phoenix: NCA Object
sources.locator: Dose types for models 200-202 and steady-state assumptions
sources.supports: The relevant infusion model assumes constant input. Together with the NCA formulas this bounds the Tinf/2 correction; interrupted or varying input requires separate treatment.

sources.title: Phoenix: Sparse sampling calculation
sources.locator: Mean concentration at unique times; nominal-time recommendation; repeated-sample correlation
sources.supports: Time handling must match sampling design. Nominal-time grouping for a sparse procedure differs from individual actual times; the software recommendation is not a universal substitution rule.

sources.title: ICH M10: Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis
sources.supports: Reported concentrations depend on a defined assay, matrix, calibration range and LLOQ, with stability and recovery assessed. The profile records whether this information exists; it does not grade an assay.

sources.title: PKNCA: Secondary parameters (renal clearance)
sources.locator: Renal clearance, start to finish; Units that differ between the two profiles
sources.supports: Renal clearance links the amount excreted in a urine collection (concentration and volume over start-end times) to plasma AUC over the same interval. Package settings are not project approval.

profiles.name: Data requirements for observed peaks and finite-window NCA
profiles.applies_when: The project requests observed peak summaries or finite-window exposure. Check input definitions, permitted source data and sampling coverage separately for each endpoint. Numerical NCA methods and result evaluation belong to the later analysis module.
required_inputs: Each requested endpoint and intended use; proposal-defined AUC window and time origin, with analyte, matrix and total/free concentration basis.
Permitted concentration-time data with units, study/profile membership and dosing context.
Source origin, data level and sampling design: original versus digitized data; individual versus group summary; serial, destructive or mixed sampling.
conditional_inputs: Dose amount and dose basis when the objective requires normalization or comparison; dosing times and single-dose, repeated-dose or verified steady-state context where they define the window.

For digitized observations: the source figure, panel/curve, axes and transformations, units, extraction provenance and any existing reconstruction review. Distinguish measured points from fitted or predicted curves.

For group summaries: arithmetic/geometric mean or median, contributing sample counts and reported SD/SE/CI definitions; variance/covariance information if uncertainty is requested. Missing uncertainty information is distinct from missing point-estimate inputs.
BLQ/LLOQ, missing-value flags and actual versus nominal time definitions where relevant. If these are unspecified, retain the ambiguity.

Bioanalytical context where reported: assay method, measured matrix (plasma, serum or blood), calibration range and LLOQ, validation status, and any reported stability, recovery or adsorption problem. Record whether this information exists; do not grade the assay.

For site-of-infection or tissue matrices: sampling method, any dilution correction (for example urea-based correction of lavage fluid), tissue mass or volume basis and units. Keep these concentrations separate from plasma or serum concentrations.
acceptable_alternatives: Digitized measured group means may be candidate data for group-level NCA. Preserve their provenance and limitations; do not manufacture individual observations.

Record available evidence or an existing reviewed plan for unobserved boundaries. If resolution requires an analytical method, mark it for the NCA module rather than selecting or testing that method here.
data_checks: Match available data to every requested endpoint. Do not infer coverage from filenames, headers, row count or the availability of another endpoint.

Require the proposal to define each AUC window by intended use, including AUCtau when relevant. Retain an undefined window as an unresolved definition; do not choose 0-24 h, infinity or a shorter observed interval by default.

List observed times, window boundaries and internal unsampled intervals. Distinguish observed, source-reported estimated and unobserved boundary values. Do not fill gaps or select integration or boundary-treatment methods.
Keep studies, regimens, matrices, individual records and group-summary curves distinct. Do not interchange arithmetic means, geometric means and medians.
Observed Cmax/Tmax refer to sampled concentrations. A group-mean curve does not establish the unobserved true peak or the mean of individual peaks.
Retain BLQ and missingness without substitution. Report unavailable uncertainty inputs separately from unavailable inputs for a point estimate.

Check that the dose basis and the measured analyte correspond: salt versus free base, mass versus activity units, and, for multi-component substances, which components the dose and the assay each refer to. A conversion factor needs a cited source; retain an unresolved basis rather than converting.

Identify the time-zero condition implied by route and input: an unobserved initial concentration after bolus dosing, the end of infusion for infusions, and pre-dose concentrations for repeated dosing. Record whether each boundary value is observed, source-assumed or unknown; leave any back-extrapolation to the NCA module.
profiles.missing_effect: Report input coverage and gaps for each requested endpoint. A missing definition or unresolved coverage prevents declaring its input requirements met; retain independent supported input matches and route method-dependent questions to NCA analysis.
not_established: Completed NCA, reliable numerical exposure or an approved integration/boundary method.
Individual trajectories, individual variability or uncertainty reconstructed from group means.
A universal sampling-count threshold or permission to replace the requested endpoint.

AUMC and MRT when explicitly requested

Late concentration-time observations with source membership, units, quantifiability and reported BLQ/LLOQ information.

Check whether endpoint and timing definitions are explicit and compatible with the source records. Do not silently change the requested exposure window.

Identify absent late data or unresolved absorption, dosing and quantifiability information. If sufficiency requires a fitted slope or extrapolation diagnostic, report it as unresolved for downstream analysis.
Assess available inputs separately for each terminal-dependent endpoint without imposing a universal point count or calculating regression, residuals or tail fractions.

not_established: A selected terminal interval, fitted lambda_z, calculated tail contribution or accepted terminal estimate.
An elimination mechanism, individual parameter distribution or human predictive validity.

Permitted concentration-time data and applicable MP001/MP002 input metadata, or a traceable permitted same-drug published estimate retained as a literature candidate.
Route, analyte-specific dose and dose basis, dosing times, regimen, units, biological matrix, total/free basis and actual data level.
conditional_inputs: For single-dose IV clearance, data covering the exposure course including late observations relevant to AUCinf. For a steady-state interval approach, evidence of steady state and a proposal-defined interval with matching dose and exposure data.

For Vss, time-course data potentially supporting the required exposure/moment information and the dosing-input history; infusion duration and whether input was constant, varying or interrupted. Single-dose data are not excluded solely because the parameter name contains steady state.
A source-supported applicable bioavailability estimate if absolute CL is requested from extravascular evidence; otherwise retain the distinction from CL/F.
Formation/systemic-input information and active-moiety or molecular-weight basis when the measured analyte is formed from the administered parent/prodrug.
Body weight when dose/parameter normalization or later scaling requires it; relevant dose-dependence information and reported uncertainty where available or required by the objective.

Characteristics of the contributing animals as reported: species, strain, sex, actual body weight, and health, infection or renal-function state. Record unreported characteristics as gaps; do not assume healthy or typical animals.
acceptable_alternatives: NCA input data or published estimates may be candidates without a compartmental fit. This does not qualify the resulting parameter for extrapolation.

When project permissions allow, same-drug published CL/Vss without original curves may enter as LITERATURE_REPORTED, NOT_RECALCULATED and NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED. Retain citation/page/table, parameter definition, study/dose context, estimation method, reported uncertainty and missing information.

A group-summary point estimate without reliable uncertainty remains a candidate with an explicit uncertainty gap. Preserve the required later human use review; do not count it as a qualified species here.
data_checks: Map inputs separately to CL and Vss; availability for one does not establish availability for the other. An available finite-window AUC does not automatically meet a request requiring exposure to infinity.
Check route, analyte input, matrix, free/total basis, weight normalization and units against the requested parameter. Do not merge incompatible definitions.
Check whether dose refers to the measured analyte or its parent/prodrug. Missing formation information may leave absolute analyte clearance unresolved while exposure data remain usable.
Preserve group-level parameter meaning, reported dose dependence and unresolved input-history information. Do not choose or test a clearance, moment or infusion-correction formula.

For a literature-only candidate, identify what is actually reported and what cannot be independently checked without underlying data. Candidate registration is not parameter validation or species qualification.
Apply the MP001 dose-basis and analyte-composition check to every dose used for a requested parameter. An unresolved basis leaves the dose-dependent inputs for that parameter unresolved.
Map Vz separately from CL and Vss: it depends on the terminal-phase inputs assessed under MP002.
profiles.missing_effect: Record which input or definition is missing for each parameter, its intended use and the required next action. Retain available candidates and independent input matches; parameter qualification and the project-specific species minimum are assessed later.
not_established: Calculated or accepted CL/Vss, a compartmental curve shape, or qualification for human extrapolation.
Absolute clearance from an extravascular dose without applicable F, or interchangeability of Vss, Vz and Vc.
A known uncertainty distribution merely because a candidate was registered or reviewed.
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions

profiles.name: Data requirements for urinary excretion and renal clearance
target_endpoints: Amount and fraction of dose excreted unchanged in urine (Ae, fe)
Nonrenal clearance by difference when explicitly requested
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action
profiles.applies_when: The project requests urinary excretion, renal clearance or a renal/nonrenal split of clearance. Reuse the MP001 and MP003 definitions for plasma exposure, dose basis and analyte; inspect only urine-specific inputs. Calculation belongs to the later analysis module.
required_inputs: Urine collection intervals with start and end times relative to dosing, and whether collection was complete for each interval.
For each interval: urine volume and analyte concentration with units, or a reported amount excreted; the analyte and its relation to the administered dose basis.
The dose, route and dose basis that fe refers to.
conditional_inputs: Plasma exposure over the same intervals when renal clearance is requested, assessed under MP001 and MP003.
Total clearance from MP003 when nonrenal clearance by difference is requested.
Metabolite or conjugate measurements in urine when the objective separates unchanged drug from metabolites.
acceptable_alternatives: Published same-drug fe or CLR may enter as LITERATURE_REPORTED, NOT_RECALCULATED and NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED when project permissions allow, with source, definition, collection duration and missing information.
data_checks: Distinguish concentrations from amounts and cumulative from interval values. Do not derive an amount without a recorded volume.
Compare the collection duration with the requested endpoint. Excretion up to the last collection is not total excretion; do not extrapolate it here.
Check that plasma and urine intervals, analytes and units correspond before matching them to renal clearance. Keep unresolved correspondence as a gap.
Record missing, pooled or incomplete collections and the experimental unit (individual animal or pooled cage) without inventing animal IDs.
profiles.missing_effect: Report the affected excretion or clearance endpoint and its missing urine input through the general data-gap policy. Missing urine data do not block plasma-based PK work.
not_established: Calculated fe, CLR or nonrenal clearance.
Complete excretion from a truncated collection, or an elimination mechanism.

profiles.name: Data requirements for animal PK modeling
target_endpoints: animal PK parameters requested by the project
profiles.applies_when: The objective requests an animal time-course model. Check the available modeling inputs and unresolved design information. Model selection, fitting and result evaluation belong to the animal PK module.
required_inputs: Requested modeling objective, parameter or curve outputs and intended use.
Permitted concentration-time observations, dosing events, route, analyte, matrix, concentration basis and units.
Study/regimen membership, sampling design, data level and available experimental-unit identifiers; identify unverifiable IDs rather than inventing them.
conditional_inputs: Infusion duration/input history, extravascular dosing information, or covariates such as body weight when required by the stated objective.
Verified individual-level records and sampling structure when individual or population variability is requested. Do not impose dense repeated sampling for every animal as a universal input rule.
Summary definition, counts and reported variability for group-summary curves; source extraction details for digitized observations; BLQ/LLOQ and missingness metadata where relevant.
Concentration-time data at more than one dose level when the objective includes characterizing dose-dependent (nonlinear) kinetics. Do not impose a number of dose levels.
acceptable_alternatives: Measured group-mean curves may be candidate inputs for exploratory group-level modeling with stated limitations, without inferred animal random effects.
Keep data potentially supporting a separate NCA objective available when modeling inputs are incomplete; do not replace the requested modeling objective silently.
data_checks: Map available concentration, timing, dose, route and grouping information to the stated modeling objective. Report actual coverage and missing phases or dose levels without a universal row-count threshold.
Distinguish individual records, destructive sampling and group summaries. Unverified cross-time IDs do not establish individual trajectories.
Keep study and regimen identities. Identify compatibility questions for later model design; do not pool incompatible sources or treat every source curve as a separate mandatory model.

If input sufficiency depends on a structural model or numerical assessment, retain the uncertainty for the animal PK module. Do not choose compartments, error models, estimation engines or diagnostic thresholds here.
profiles.missing_effect: Report available modeling inputs, task-specific gaps and the data or clarification needed. A positive input assessment permits the next preparation/design step only and does not approve fitting or its results.
not_established: An accepted structural model, convergence, parameter identifiability, uncertainty or a valid human prediction.
Animal IIV from group means or unverified IDs.
Automatic preference for additional compartments or a completed model comparison.
